sources.note: Inserts optimizable latent states at an intermediate Transformer layer rather than at the output, so self-attention makes every continuation token's log-probability differentiable with respect to every latent and reward-weighted gradients reach them from the whole continuation instead of only through their own decoded token.
sources.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning

sources.note: Shows that the part of a steering vector which breaks a model's refusal behaviour is a separate direction from the part that produces the intended behavioural effect, and learns that direction by constrained optimization so it can be ablated without losing the steering.
sources.title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible

sources.note: Replaces the single tolerance threshold that RLVR uses to score floating-point answers with a hybrid reward pairing a hard clinical-safety constraint against a continuous precision-sensitive term, and adds a reward for stating the computational formula explicitly so an external verifier can check it.
sources.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Trains self-correction as a step-level preference problem -- preferring a detect-and-repair continuation over the continuation that would follow if the error went unaddressed -- after first initialising with ordinary step-level preference optimisation, and finds that correcting more often and detecting more errors both anti-correlate with accuracy.
sources.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

sources.note: Names and measures a multilingual tool-calling failure in which the model picks the right API but writes argument values in the wrong language, then compares supervised fine-tuning against PPO and GRPO under matched budgets and finds that a well-selected supervised checkpoint matches or beats reinforcement learning on the task while costing more elsewhere.
sources.title: When the API Speaks the Wrong Language: Revisiting Post-Training for Multilingual Tool Use

sources.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
sources.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

result.definition: A 14B instruction-tuned Qwen2.5 model, used across 6 sources as the larger arm in comparisons whose smaller arm is the 7B instruct model -- the pair that lets a method's scale dependence be checked within one family and generation. Two archived results attach to it. In a self-correction study it is among the newer, stronger backbones where the method's gains shrink, attributed to those models already self-correcting before training. And in a multilingual tool-use study it is the size at which the supervised baseline is ahead of reinforcement learning (74.47 against 71.08) while at 7B the ordering reverses, which is that source's evidence that the ordering is not monotone in size. It also appears as a steering-vector subject and as a training backbone for medical and entropy-dynamics work.
